newsitem.title: CUBA: Four leading Cuban dissidents detained.
newsitem.headline: Four leading Cuban dissidents detained.

text.p: Four leading Cuban dissidents who run a small opposition group on the Communist-ruled island have been detained by Cuban state security, diplomatic and dissident sources said on Thursday.
State security officers detained Vladimiro Roca, Martha Beatriz Roque, Felix Bonne and Rene Gomez Manzano at their Havana homes early on Wednesday, the sources said.

The four run a small organisation called the "Working Group of Internal Dissidence," a group that says it has the support of 14 other small Cuban dissident movements. The Working Group, which is seeking some unity among Cuba's fragmented and illegal opposition, has been increasingly seeking to draw attention to itself abroad in recent months.
Authorities also detained on Wednesday a dissident journalist called Luis Lopez Prendes, the sources said. His detention did not appear related to the Working Group members.

Cuban authorities had no immediate comment on the cases, but President Fidel Castro's government rarely comments on the activities of dissident groups. Authorities call the groups "grupusculos," tiny bodies with no significance, and say they are puppets of a U.S. policy seeking to destroy Cuba.
The diplomatic and dissident sources said it was not clear if any of those detained had been charged.
But Roca's wife, Magaly de Armas, told reporters at the couple's home that her husband had been told he was under investigation.
She said state security officials arrived before dawn on Wednesday to take Roca away and then conducted an eight-hour search of the house, confiscating piles of possessions.

The confiscated material included 132 books, papers related to Roca's dissident work, a computer and computer printer, a typewriter, a video camera, a tape recorder, an English language course and dozens of pens and pencils, de Armas said.

Dissident sources said similar searches were carried out at the houses of Bonne and Gomez Manzano. Security officials confiscated a computer, three typewriters and numerous documents from Gomez Manzano's house, one dissident source said. They took two tape recorders and other office material from Bonne's house, the source added.
The Working Group has held two news conferences for foreign journalists since May, which is unusual.

At the most recent of these, last month, the group presented a paper sharply criticising a document prepared by the Communist Party for nationwide discussion ahead of the party's Congress this October.

It did not appear the detentions of the four members of the Working Group were related to the bombing of two Havana hotels last Saturday. The Interior Ministry has said it has evidence the two small bombs, which slightly injured three people, were planted by people who came from the United States. The ministry has not given details of this evidence.
Roca, asked about the bombings at the weekend, was quick to strongly condemn them, saying he was against all terrorism.

But one dissident source said dissident journalist Lopez Prendes may have been detained because he made comments to the foreign media shortly after the bombs went off at the Nacional and Capri hotels in central Havana.

One dissident source said the round-up was possibly a preventative government measure ahead of an international leftist youth festival to be held in Havana July 28-Aug. 5, which more than 5,000 young people are expected to attend.
